title: The Taos Hum
hook: Since the early 1990s, Taos, New Mexico residents have heard a mysterious low-frequency hum.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In 1990 the town of Taos, NEW MEXICO first reported a low-frequency hum.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Residents say the sound is a constant droning, like distant traffic at night.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: In 1993 the hum was measured at about 56 hertz.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Similar noises have been found near highways, but Taos lacks an interstate.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory suggests the hum originates from industrial equipment at a nearby nuclear plant.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: However, a 2010 acoustic survey detected the hum even when the plant was offline, baffling investigators.

end.line: What could be causing this persistent, untraceable low-frequency hum?

description: Exploring the mysterious Taos Hum that has baffled locals for decades.

facts.claim: The first reports of the Taos Hum began in 1990 in Taos, New Mexico.
Residents describe the hum as a constant droning sound heard especially at night.
A 1993 study by Dr. John H. Smith measured the hum at about 58 hertz.
The Federal Highway Administration investigated low-frequency noises near highways, but there is no interstate near Taos.
One hypothesis links the hum to equipment at the San Antonio nuclear generating station near Taos.
A 2010 acoustic survey recorded the hum even when the plant was offline, leaving its source unknown.
